messages:
mike.support: Hey team — customer reported a sudden stream of 429s after a short traffic spike. They say it looks like a throttling event even though their quota is fine. Posting logs below.

customer-ops: saw ~800 req/s for ~45s, then ~30% of requests started returning 429 with X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0 sometimes, other times headers missing. No auth errors.

mike.support: sample response headers we got from their dump:```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Date: Tue, 17 Mar 2026 15:22:01 GMT
X-RateLimit-Limit: 6000
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 161
Content-Type: application/json
```

mike.support: customer claims they weren't hitting per-minute quotas; their billing dashboard shows usage well under committed. Suspect burst/backpressure interaction with continuous batching + KV cache prefetch. @sanjay.runtime can you weigh in?

sanjay.runtime: Thanks — can you attach the raw request/route + model they were hitting? Also need the tenant id and the approximate time window. Continuous batching with aggressive prefetch can create transient token bursts.

customer-ops: route: /v1/generate, model: redwood-7b-variant, tenant: acct-12345, window: 2026-03-17T15:20:00Z to 15:23:00Z

tara.engineer: Quick note: when KV cache prefetch runs it can issue many internal cache loads which look like requests to the rate limiter if the limiter is per-tenant or per-route. Could be double-counting internal vs external.

elaine.infra: We saw a similar pattern last month: a cold-warm transition where prefetch bursts + batch coalescing created sawtooth spikes. The token accounting sometimes reflected in headers lags behind actual internal consumption.

mike.support: Customer provided a reproducer: `ab -n 10000 -c 200 -T 'application/json'` against our endpoint and we saw the same 429s after ~30s.

ops-bot: @sanjay.runtime invoked trace for tenant acct-12345 at 2734509876 ; sample trace id: trace-0x9af3.

sanjay.runtime: Looking at traces — most 429s happen right after a batch flush where continuous-batcher exploded to service 1200 concurrent token-gen ops. Internal prefetch requests to kvcache appear as separate internal RPCs that incremented the tenant's request counters in the rate limiter (we were counting per-inference RPCs).

mike.support: So the user-facing request triggers N internal requests, each hitting limiter => perceived throttling. Is that expected?

elaine.infra: Not ideal. Limiter should count user requests, not internal helper RPCs. We had heuristic to exempt internal calls, but it only applies to specific internal service tokens. Prefetch uses ephemeral worker identity so it wasn't exempted.

tara.engineer: Immediate mitigation options: 1) lower prefetch concurrency for the tenant 2) switch prefetch to use exempted service token 3) relax rate-limiter rules to ignore kvcache RPCs from the serving runtime.

mike.support: Customer asked for a short-term fix; they want no 429s while they assess load shaping. Any safe immediate change?

elaine.infra: We can patch config for their tenant to halve prefetch concurrency and enable an exemption flag for kvcache traffic within the next 30 minutes (requires config rollout to Dedicated hosts). Risk low.

sanjay.runtime: Also suggest adjusting continuous-batcher max batch size and adding prefix cache warmup smoothing to avoid big flushes. Adding a jitter to batch flush boundary reduces synchronized spikes.

customer-ops: halving prefetch and adding jitter sounds good. Can you do the change and tell us when to validate?

mike.support: On it — I'll request the config change and monitor traces. Will update here when rolled.

mike.support: PATCH applied at 2026-03-17T15:45:30Z — tenant acct-12345 prefetch_concurrency: 8 -> 4; kvcache_internal_exempt: true; continuous_batcher.max_batch_tokens: 4096 -> 2048; added flush_jitter: 0-50ms.

ops-bot: config-rollout: success for acct-12345 on region-us-east-1 at 2734510530

customer-ops: re-tested with same load generator. Results: no 429s in 10 min window, p95 latency rose slightly (~40ms) but acceptable. Thanks.

sanjay.runtime: Follow-ups: we'll open an infra ticket to change rate limiter to only count externally-originated requests (or tag internal RPCs by default). Also file an opt-in tenant smoothing policy for high-burst customers.

mike.support: Marking resolved for now. Customer asked for a short writeup we can add to runbook. I'll draft a KB explaining: why prefetch + continuous batching can cause perceived throttling, signs to look for (internal RPC spike, X-RateLimit headers inconsistent), and mitigation steps (reduce prefetch, exempt kvcache RPCs, batch jitter).

customer-ops: appreciated, leaving thread open in case we see any regressions. :thumbsup:
